prompt: An experimenter divides a total measured mass of $3.6\text{ kg}$ equally among 12 identical samples. Calculate the mass of one sample, stating both the numerical magnitude and the unit.
answer: Mass of one sample = 0.30 kg (numerical magnitude 0.30, unit kg).

mark_scheme.criterion: Shows division of total mass by 12: 3.6 / 12.
0.30 kg (or 0.3 kg); both numerical value and unit required for A1 mark.

hints: Ensure your final answer includes the unit kg.
solution:
Mass of one sample = (3.6 kg) / 12 = 0.30 kg.
The numerical magnitude is 0.30 and the unit is kilograms (kg).
teacher_walkthrough: Accuracy mark strictly requires the unit 'kg'.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored as an original drill on division with units.
